content.value_statement: Difficult workplace conversations often fail when people enter them angry, vague, or unprepared. This skill gives structured preparation, scripts, and follow-up steps for clearer outcomes.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through preparation, delivery, and follow-up steps for workplace conversations.
Uses the Situation-Behavior-Impact model to shape feedback around observable facts.
Provides opening lines and response phrases for conflict, feedback, and sensitive topics.
Helps users separate facts, interpretations, emotions, and desired outcomes.
Offers emotional regulation techniques for before, during, and after conversations.
Supports follow-up planning with agreements, timelines, and check-in points.
limitations: Does not replace legal, HR, medical, or mental health advice.
Cannot verify facts or workplace policies without user-provided context.
May not fit highly regulated, union, or formal disciplinary processes.
Requires the user to adapt scripts to the relationship and workplace culture.

use_cases.title: Prepare Performance Feedback
use_cases.description: Plan a clear conversation about missed expectations, support needs, and next steps.

use_cases.title: Resolve Peer Conflict
use_cases.description: Turn hurt, frustration, or tension into a focused conversation about behavior and impact.

use_cases.title: Coach Sensitive Discussions
use_cases.description: Help employees prepare for compensation, escalation, or relationship repair conversations.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Basic Conversation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner preparation for one workplace issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare for a difficult workplace conversation. The issue is [issue], the person is [role], and my goal is [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Turn Facts Into SBI Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert a concern into Situation-Behavior-Impact language.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SBI model for this feedback: [facts]. Help me remove assumptions and write a respectful opening.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Responses to Defensiveness
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare for likely reactions during the conversation.
prompt_templates.prompt: I expect the other person may react defensively by [reaction]. Help me prepare calm responses and redirect to shared goals.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Full Conversation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a high-stakes workplace discussion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full plan for this conversation: context [context], power dynamics [details], risks [risks], desired outcome [outcome], and follow-up needs [needs].

output_examples.input: I need to address three missed deadlines with a teammate.
output: Clarified issue: three recent deliverables were late and blocked project work.
Suggested opening: I want to discuss the recent timelines and understand what is getting in the way.
Next step: agree on prevention steps, support needed, and a check-in date.

output_examples.input: A peer criticized my work in a meeting and I felt embarrassed.
output: Fact: the peer criticized the work during the meeting.
Impact: you felt embarrassed and trust was damaged.
Opening: I want to talk about yesterday. I would like feedback shared in a way that helps us improve.

output_examples.input: I want to ask my manager for a raise but I am nervous.
output: Preparation focus: clarify contributions, market context, and timing.
Suggested opening: I would like to discuss my compensation and how it reflects my current responsibilities.
Follow-up: ask for a decision timeline or the criteria for a future adjustment.

best_practices: Separate observable facts from assumptions before drafting any opening line.
State the impact clearly and invite the other person to share their view.
Leave the conversation with specific agreements, owners, and follow-up timing.
anti_patterns: Do not script every word or build a legal-style case to win the conversation.
Do not start with character judgments, blame, or phrases like you always.
Do not skip follow-up after agreement, especially when behavior change is expected.

faq.question: Can this skill handle performance feedback?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps structure feedback around facts, impact, expectations, support, and follow-up.

faq.question: Does it replace HR guidance?
faq.answer: No. Use HR, legal, or policy guidance for formal discipline, harassment, safety, or compliance matters.

faq.question: Can it help when I am angry?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes emotional readiness checks and regulation steps before you choose words.

faq.question: Does it write exact scripts?
faq.answer: It can draft openings and phrases, but it recommends themes over memorized scripts.

faq.question: Can individual contributors use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports peer conflict, upward feedback, compensation talks, and relationship repair.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Share the facts, impact, relationship, desired outcome, and any workplace constraints.
